name: Blackcurrant (juice and extract)
short: Extract or supplement by mouth, 7-day trials in 49 trained adults: no adverse events, or events like placebo. Juice in 12 healthy men raised urine oxalate (a stone risk factor).
text: The adverse-event data found are for blackcurrant extract or supplements, not juice. In a 7-day randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial in 29 male elite taekwondo athletes taking New Zealand blackcurrant extract, no adverse events were reported. In a randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled crossover trial in 20 resistance-trained adults who took low- or high-dose New Zealand blackcurrant supplements for 7 days in each condition, adverse events were comparable across all conditions and both doses were well tolerated over the short supplementation period. For the juice, a study in 12 healthy men on a standardised diet who drank 330 ml of blackcurrant juice in place of mineral water found raised urine pH and citric acid excretion and also raised oxalic acid excretion; the study was about kidney-stone risk factors and does not report adverse events. No interaction data were found in the cited sources.
